points.t: A firm, slowly enlarging plaque on the trunk or shoulder that later becomes lumpy (protuberant).
A low-grade fibroblastic sarcoma driven by a COL1A1–PDGFB gene fusion.
Refer on a suspected sarcoma or skin-cancer pathway; deep biopsy; Mohs or wide excision; imatinib for inoperable disease.
Delayed diagnosis because it is called a scar, keloid or dermatofibroma for years.

points: Over 90% carry the translocation **t(17;22)** (often as a ring chromosome), fusing **COL1A1–PDGFB**. This drives autocrine PDGF receptor stimulation and is the rationale for **imatinib** in unresectable or metastatic disease.
Histology: storiform spindle cells infiltrating fat in a "honeycomb" pattern; **CD34 positive, Factor XIIIa negative** (contrast DF).
Adults aged 20–50; trunk (especially chest and shoulder), proximal limbs, head and neck.

Starts as a slowly enlarging, firm, skin-coloured, pink-violet or brown **indurated plaque**, often mistaken for a scar, keloid, morphoea or DF for years, the same lesion a year apart). Later it becomes **protuberant and multinodular**.

Variants: pigmented (Bednar tumour), atrophic (looks like morphoea), and childhood/congenital forms. The the [skin cancer](condition:basal-cell-carcinoma) notes the course summary notes DFSP can **mimic a keloidal BCC**.
Deep incisional or punch biopsy that includes subcutis (shave biopsies miss it). CD34 immunohistochemistry; FISH/RT-PCR for COL1A1–PDGFB when needed.
MRI for large or recurrent tumours to define deep extent. Chest imaging only for fibrosarcomatous or metastatic disease (specialist).

items.t: A ‘dermatofibroma’ or ‘keloid’ that keeps growing, is larger than about 3 cm or becomes nodular: refer to exclude **DFSP**.

pearls.t: "A keloid without an injury is not a keloid until proved otherwise."
Imatinib interactions (CYP3A4; warfarin; paracetamol hepatotoxicity at high doses) are worth knowing if a patient on it presents to primary care.
